caption: A garment steamer is run slowly down a wrinkled shirt hanging on a rail, and the creases relax and drop out where the steam passes.

sa.check: A wrinkled shirt hangs on a rail.
A steamer head is moved down the shirt.
Steam rises from the steamer head.
The creases drop out where the head has passed.
The fabric darkens where it is damp.
The steaming comes first and the smoothing follows.

pc.expect: The fabric smooths only along the path the head has taken, and wrinkles away from that path stay.
pc.fail: The whole shirt smooths at once while the head is at one spot; or creases drop out on a part of the shirt the head never reached; or the head passes over a crease and the fabric behind it is unchanged; or the shirt smooths before any steam appears.

pc.expect: Creases only drop out and smoothed fabric stays smooth.
pc.fail: A crease comes back on fabric the head has just passed over; or the fabric wrinkles more where the head has been; or the fabric dries and creases again while the steamer works on it; or the shirt smooths and wrinkles in turn.

pc.expect: The steam rises from the head and the shirt hangs downward from the rail, its hem swinging and settling.
pc.fail: The steam pours downward through the shirt; or sinks and pools on the floor; or the shirt's hem rises and stays up with nothing lifting it; or the shirt lifts off the rail.

pc.expect: The shirt is cloth that hangs, sways and relaxes as it dampens, and the steamer head is a rigid tool.
pc.fail: The shirt stays board-stiff and keeps its shape as the head passes; or the fabric stretches like elastic under the head; or the head bends or droops; or the shirt sticks to the head and lifts with it.

pc.expect: One shirt on one rail and one steamer head; the shirt stays on its hanger and nothing passes through it.
pc.fail: The head passes through the shirt; or a second shirt appears; or the shirt vanishes; or the shirt's collar or sleeve detaches.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The shirt's colour and pattern, the rail and the room stay the same.
pc.fail: The shirt changes colour or pattern; or the rail changes shape; or items in the room rearrange.
